project.name: Payday
project.description: What is safe to spend until payday, and when the loans end.

phases.name: Walking skeleton
phases.goal: A number read from the real database appears on the deployed app, installed on an iPhone and an Android phone, with its data backed up and the performance budget measured.
phases.demo: "This is the app on my home screen: tap, and the number from the database is there — and here is that same database restored from backup."

exitCriteria.text: From a fresh clone, `cd app && pnpm install && pnpm dev` starts the app, and the home route shows a number read from SQLite through a migrated table. — verified 2026-10-31 on a clean copy of `app/`: 412.50 shown 14 s after install began
CI is green on a real Vitest unit test and a real Playwright test.
A new contributor gets from clone to running in under 15 minutes by following `app/README.md`. — verified 2026-10-31 by the same walk-through, following the README; not yet timed by a person
The JavaScript shipped for the home screen is measured from the production build and recorded in `SPECS.md`. — 33.5 KB gzipped against 60 KB, by budget.e2e.ts, 2026-10-31
The app is deployed and reachable over HTTPS — at release
It installs to the home screen and opens full-screen on an iPhone and an Android phone — at release
A restore from object storage into a fresh volume brings back a row written before the drill — at release
Every `SPECS.md` performance budget is measured on both phones against production and the numbers recorded — at release

nonGoals: Sign-in, any real financial data, any feature screen. The deployed skeleton holds only fictional data until Phase 1's sign-in exists.

phases.name: Safe to spend
phases.goal: Starting from nothing, the owner enters their pay, bills and loan payments in under 20 minutes and sees, behind a passkey, what is safe to spend until the next payday.
phases.demo: "I set up my pay and bills from scratch in fifteen minutes. This is what I can spend until Friday, and this is everything already spoken for."

exitCriteria.text: Every route except sign-in redirects to sign-in without a session, proven by a Playwright test that visits them all. — auth.e2e.ts over every route in tests/support/routes.ts, 2026-10-31
A passkey registered on one device signs in on the other phone and the laptop, by adding a second passkey or the cross-device flow.

For the fixture household, the safe-to-spend number matches a hand calculation on five named dates — including a payday itself, a month-end and a three-paycheck month — in unit tests. — safeToSpend.test.ts, 2026-10-31
Someone who did not build it completes first-run setup for the fixture household in under 20 minutes, timed, ending on the number.
The home screen shows the number, the next payday and what is reserved, at phone and laptop sizes. — home.e2e.ts on the iphone, android and laptop projects, 2026-10-31

The performance budget is re-checked with five years of generated data, and the numbers recorded. — performance.test.ts: p95 22.3 ms locally for 40 items and 600 overrides; home JavaScript 39.1 KB; recorded in SPECS.md, 2026-10-31
The owner's real pay, bills and loan payments are entered on production — at release

nonGoals: The check-in, reminders, loan balances and interest, any per-expense logging.

phases.name: Payday check-in
phases.goal: On payday the phone reminds the owner, and a five-minute check-in turns the new balance into what was spent and a plan for the next 14 days.
phases.demo: "It's payday. The phone buzzed, I tapped it, confirmed my pay and balance — that's what I spent these two weeks — and this is what the next paycheck has to cover."

exitCriteria.text: A Playwright test completes a check-in at phone size: pay confirmed, balance entered, spending shown, payments confirmed, plan shown. — checkin.e2e.ts on WebKit at iPhone size, 2026-10-31

For the fixture household, spending since the last check-in equals expected minus actual balance, and a payment marked missed stays reserved, in unit tests. — domain/checkin.test.ts, checkin.test.ts, 2026-10-31
The next six paychecks each show what they must cover, and a fixture paycheck that cannot cover its bills is flagged with the shortfall. — domain/plan.test.ts, phase2.e2e.ts, 2026-10-31
A check-in on the fixture household takes five minutes or less by stopwatch, from opening the reminder to the plan shown.
A payday reminder arrives on an installed iPhone and an Android phone at the chosen time and opens the check-in — at release
The owner completes the first real payday check-in on their phone — at release

nonGoals: Loan balances and the debt-free date, payoff strategies, categories, imports.

phases.name: Loans and debt-free date
phases.goal: Every loan, of all four kinds, is on one screen with the total owed, the interest it costs each month and the date it will all be paid off — kept true at every check-in.
phases.demo: "This is everything I owe: this much in total, costing me this much a month in interest, and at this pace I'm free on this date. After today's check-in, it's this much lower."

exitCriteria.text: A credit card, an instalment loan, a buy-now-pay-later plan and an informal loan can each be entered with the fields their kind needs. — loans.test.ts, loans.e2e.ts, 2026-10-31
Each kind's payoff projection matches a reference calculation within one minor unit per period, in unit tests. — loans.test.ts, checked after every period, 2026-10-31
A loan whose payment does not cover its interest shows that it will never be paid off at this pace, instead of a date. — loans.test.ts, loans.e2e.ts, 2026-10-31
Loan payments are counted once in the safe-to-spend number, proven by a fixture test that converts a bill into a loan. — loans.test.ts, 2026-10-31
A check-in pre-fills each loan's expected balance, and a credit card's balance change counts toward spending. — checkinLoans.test.ts, loans.e2e.ts, 2026-10-31

The performance budget is re-checked with five years of generated data, and the numbers recorded. — performance.test.ts: home p95 30–63 ms and loans p95 57–70 ms locally with 8 loans and 130 check-ins; recorded in SPECS.md, 2026-10-31
The owner's real loans are entered on production and the debt-free date is shown — at release

nonGoals: Comparing payoff strategies ([[Debt Payoff Planner]]), refinancing what-ifs, imports.

phases.name: Paycheck list export
phases.goal: Any of the next six paychecks downloads as a text file, a PDF or a Word document laid out exactly as the owner's handwritten list, with what is optional and what is already paid marked.
phases.demo: "This is my list for Friday's salary: same as I write it, with the paid ones ticked. Here it is as a PDF."

exitCriteria.text: The owner's sample list reproduces line for line from the fixture, with every total computed, in a unit test. — domain/paycheckList.test.ts, 2026-11-01
A bill marked paid on the plan is ticked at the next check-in, and marking bills paid or optional leaves the safe-to-spend number unchanged, in tests. — money/paycheckList.test.ts, 2026-11-01
A Playwright test downloads the text file, the PDF and the Word document and checks their contents. — export.e2e.ts on WebKit, Android and laptop; marks.e2e.ts at iPhone size, 2026-11-01
The three files open in Notepad, a PDF viewer and Word on the owner's laptop.
A download from the installed app works on an iPhone and an Android phone — at release

nonGoals: Spending categories, spreadsheets, a monthly list, sharing links, any change to the safe-to-spend number.

epics.title: Backups And Restore Drill
epics.theme: Paycheck And Bills Out Of Sync

tasks.text: The production SQLite file is replicated continuously to S3-compatible object storage
A written restore drill rebuilds the database from the backup into a fresh volume, and a row written before the drill is there afterwards
A health endpoint reports the age of the last successful replication

epics.title: Installable App Shell
epics.theme: Paycheck And Bills Out Of Sync

tasks.text: A web app manifest and icons make the app installable, and it opens full-screen from the home screen on iPhone and Android
A service worker caches the app shell, so the installed app opens with no network and says it is offline
tasks.description: verified by offline.e2e.ts on WebKit and Chromium, in the browser rather than installed

tasks.text: Colour, type and spacing tokens live as CSS custom properties in one file, with light and dark themes whose text meets WCAG AA contrast
tasks.description: verified by tokens.test.ts, 12 text pairs at 4.5:1 or more

tasks.text: The performance budget is measured — JavaScript per route from the production build, cold and warm opens on both phones over 4G — and recorded in `SPECS.md`

epics.title: Walking Skeleton Deployed
epics.theme: Paycheck And Bills Out Of Sync

tasks.text: A SvelteKit and TypeScript app is scaffolded in `app/` with the official `sv` scaffolder, versions pinned by the lockfile
One drizzle-kit migration creates one table, and the home route reads one row from SQLite and renders it
One Vitest unit test and one Playwright test pass locally
tasks.description: verified: 30 Vitest and 23 Playwright tests pass at iPhone, Android and laptop sizes

tasks.text: An unexpected server error shows a plain error page, and is logged with a request id
CI runs install, lint, typecheck, unit, e2e and build on every push, and is green
A Docker image runs the built app with the database file on a mounted volume
A push to main deploys the image to the host, reachable over HTTPS
`app/README.md` takes a new contributor from clone to running in under 15 minutes
tasks.description: verified by a walk-through from a clean copy of `app/`, 14 s with a warm package cache; not yet timed by a person

epics.title: Guided First Run Setup
epics.theme: Paycheck And Bills Out Of Sync

tasks.text: Setup asks for the payday and pay amount, the current balance, then each bill and loan payment one at a time, and ends on the safe-to-spend number
tasks.description: verified by journey.e2e.ts at iPhone size on WebKit

tasks.text: Setup can be left and resumed at the same step, on another device
tasks.description: verified by journey.e2e.ts, resumed in a new browser context

tasks.text: Each step has a plain-words prompt and an example, written for someone who has never budgeted
Someone who did not build it completes setup for the fixture household in under 20 minutes, timed

epics.title: Paycheck Periods And Safe To Spend
epics.theme: Paycheck And Bills Out Of Sync

tasks.text: Pay periods are derived from the payday anchor; each occurrence belongs to the paycheck that covers it, and one due on a payday counts against the previous paycheck

Safe to spend is the current balance minus everything due before the next payday minus set-asides, and matches hand calculations for the fixture on five named dates, including a payday and a three-paycheck month
tasks.description: verified by safeToSpend.test.ts, five hand-calculated dates

tasks.text: The home screen shows the number, the next payday and the list of what is reserved
The number shows the date of the balance behind it, and warns once that balance is older than the last payday
A negative result shows what is short and by how much, not a red number alone

epics.title: Private Single User Access
epics.theme: Paycheck And Bills Out Of Sync

tasks.text: The first visit registers the owner with a password (typed twice), and registration is closed from then on; a passkey can be added afterwards but is optional
tasks.description: verified by passkeys.test.ts, auth.setup.ts; a setup code guards the first registration in production (amended 2026-11-01, ADR-0010)

tasks.text: Password sign-in works on both phones and the laptop, and a passkey ("this device's PIN, fingerprint or face") is an optional extra that can be added and removed from a signed-in device (amended 2026-11-01, ADR-0010)
One-time recovery codes are shown once at registration, stored hashed, and each signs in exactly once
Sessions live on the server behind HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookies, and expire after a set idle time
tasks.description: verified by session.test.ts, auth.e2e.ts; __Host-session with Secure proven over https

tasks.text: A Playwright test confirms every route except sign-in redirects to sign-in without a session
tasks.description: verified by guard.test.ts and auth.e2e.ts over every route in tests/support/routes.ts

tasks.text: Security headers — a content security policy, HSTS and frame-ancestors — are set and checked by a test
tasks.description: verified by auth.e2e.ts; strict CSP with a nonce, no unsafe-inline

epics.title: Schedule Of Pay And Bills
epics.theme: Paycheck And Bills Out Of Sync

tasks.text: Money is stored and computed as integer minor units, enforced by a branded type, with no floats anywhere in the engine
tasks.description: verified by money.test.ts, including a grep for parseFloat and toFixed

tasks.text: Repeat rules — every 14 days from an anchor, monthly on a day, quarterly, yearly — expand into dated occurrences, and a day 29 to 31 falls on the month's last day when it is shorter
Paychecks, bills and loan payments can be added, edited and ended at phone and laptop sizes
A single occurrence can be skipped or changed without changing its rule
Yearly and quarterly bills set aside an equal share from each paycheck before they fall due
A seed script loads a fictional household that the tests and demos share
tasks.description: verified by seed.test.ts; pnpm seed loads the fixture

epics.title: Paycheck Plan View
epics.theme: Paycheck And Bills Out Of Sync

tasks.text: The next six paychecks each list what they must cover and what is left
A paycheck that cannot cover its bills is flagged with the shortfall
Months with a third paycheck are labelled
A check-in asks whether the pay landed and for how much, then the current balance
It shows the expected balance, the actual balance, and the difference as spending since the last check-in
Each scheduled payment since the last check-in is confirmed paid or marked missed, and a missed payment stays reserved
tasks.description: verified by domain/checkin.test.ts, server checkin.test.ts, checkin.e2e.ts

tasks.text: It ends on the plan for the next 14 days and the new safe-to-spend number
Each check-in is saved with its date, numbers and duration, and past check-ins are listed
A Playwright test completes a check-in at phone size
tasks.description: verified by checkin.e2e.ts at iPhone size on WebKit

tasks.text: The installed app subscribes to push reminders on iPhone and Android, after a prompt that says why
A reminder is sent on each payday at the chosen time, and tapping it opens the check-in
tasks.description: verified by job.test.ts (fake clock and sender) and serviceWorker.test.ts; delivery to a real phone is checked at release

tasks.text: An expired or rejected subscription is removed, and the app shows that reminders are off
A calendar file with every payday can be downloaded as a fallback reminder

epics.title: Debt Free Date Projection
sources: Loan Ledger With Debt Free Date

tasks.text: Each kind of loan projects its payoff date at current payments, matching a reference calculation within one minor unit per period, in unit tests
tasks.description: verified by loans.test.ts, against the closed-form amortisation after every period, for every kind

tasks.text: The interest all loans cost this month is shown as one figure
The overall debt-free date is shown, and a loan whose payment does not cover its interest says it will never be paid off at this pace

epics.title: Loan Balances At Check-In
sources: Loan Ledger With Debt Free Date

tasks.text: Each check-in pre-fills every loan's expected balance and lets it be confirmed or corrected
A credit card's balance change counts toward spending since the last check-in, so card purchases are no longer missed
The total owed at each check-in is listed, newest first, with the change since the previous one

epics.title: Loan Ledger
sources: Loan Ledger With Debt Free Date

tasks.text: Credit cards, instalment loans, buy-now-pay-later plans and informal loans can each be added with the fields their kind needs
A loan's payments are linked to its schedule item, so the safe-to-spend number counts each payment once
tasks.description: verified by loans.test.ts, which converts a bill into a loan and leaves the number unchanged, and loans.e2e.ts

tasks.text: A loan-payment bill entered during setup can be turned into a loan without entering it again
The loan list shows each balance, rate, next payment and due date, and the total owed

epics.title: Paid Optional And Grouped Bills
epics.theme: Paycheck And Bills Out Of Sync

tasks.text: On the Schedule page, a bill or loan payment can be given a group name and marked optional, and a migration leaves every existing item ungrouped and required
On the Plan, each bill in a paycheck can be marked paid and unmarked, without JavaScript
tasks.description: verified by money/paycheckList.test.ts, marks.e2e.ts; the Plan page sends no script

tasks.text: The next check-in starts with every bill marked paid already ticked, and a check-in's answer outranks the mark
tasks.description: verified by money/paycheckList.test.ts, the later word winning by time

tasks.text: Marking a bill optional or paid leaves the safe-to-spend number unchanged, in a fixture test
A Playwright test groups a bill, marks one optional and one paid, at phone size
tasks.description: verified by marks.e2e.ts on WebKit at iPhone size

blockers.title: No project repository, so CI has never run
blockers.nextAction: Create the project's own private repository (not tateru.dev), push the work to a branch, and watch .github/workflows/app.yml run.

blockers.title: Docker image never built
blockers.nextAction: Let Fly's remote builder build it on the first /ship, or build it locally once Docker may be used: cd app && docker build .

blockers.title: Domain not chosen
blockers.nextAction: Choose the domain before /ship; register the owner there with a password and OWNER_SETUP_CODE.

blockers.title: Checks only a person with real phones can do
blockers.nextAction: After /ship: sign in with the password on both phones (and optionally add each phone's PIN or face), turn reminders on from the installed app, have setup timed by someone else, and time a check-in under five minutes.
